channel.title: TuskersLk | ඇත් පියස Feed
channel.description: Chronicles and conservation records of Sri Lanka's notable elephants and tuskers.

item.title: Kawanthissa (The Siyambalangamuwa Giant) (කාවන්තිස්ස)
item.description: Standing nearly 11 feet tall, Kawanthissa was one of the largest and most beloved wild tuskers in modern Sri Lankan history. Known for his astonishingly peaceful demeanor around farming villages in Galgamuwa and Maho, his tragic demise in October 2026 united the nation in grief and ignited the movement to catalog and defend every surviving tusker. Roaming territory: Usgala Siyambalangamuwa, Galgamuwa and Maho. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Towering 11 ft shoulder height, thick majestic symmetrical ivory tusks, calm and dignified wild temperament.

item.title: Galgamuwa Dala Poottuwa (ගල්ගමුවේ දළ පූට්ටුවා)
item.description: Sri Lanka most recognizable wild tusker with unique crossed tusks forming an X shape. Despite suffering from blindness in one eye due to past trap gun injuries, he roamed the Galgamuwa dry zone peacefully for decades. Roaming territory: Galgamuwa and Sorabora Reserve, North Western Province. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Distinctive criss-crossed tusks, imposing stature, known for peaceful coexistence with rural farmers.

item.title: Walagamba of Kala Wewa (වලගම්බා)
item.description: Named after ancient monarch King Walagamba, renowned as one of the largest dominant alpha tuskers recorded in the North Central tank basins. His commanding presence and calm intelligence around Kala Wewa influenced tusker genetics across the region. Roaming territory: Kala Wewa and Galgamuwa, North Central Province. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Massive broad skull, thick symmetrical down-pointing tusks, deep ear pigmentation.

item.title: Panamure Hasthi Rajaya (පනාමුරේ ඇත් රජා)
item.description: The immortal symbol of freedom in Sri Lankan folklore. His heroic stand to protect his herd and refusal to yield to chains forced parliament to outlaw the elephant kraal capture system forever. Roaming territory: Panamure Forest, Sabaragamuwa Province. Status: Historical. Physical traits: Fierce herd protector, defiant wild bull immortalized in traditional folk songs and popular culture.

item.title: Thirappane Agbo (තිරප්පනේ අග්බෝ)
item.description: Beloved icon of the Rajarata wilderness. Survived debilitating trap gun and rifle wounds to his front leg thanks to an unprecedented multi-month medical mobilization by wildlife veterinarians and loving villagers. Roaming territory: Thirappane and Maradankadawala, North Central Province. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Long curving ivory tusks, resilient spirit, recognized by wildlife trackers across Anuradhapura tanks.

item.title: Kala Wewa Revatha (කලාවැවේ රේවත)
item.description: The beloved gentle giant of the Kala Wewa tank ecosystem. Thousands of nature photographers and local families visited Kala Wewa each dry season specifically to view Revatha feeding peacefully among lotus beds. Roaming territory: Kala Wewa and Balalu Wewa Sanctuary. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Dark black pigmentation, thick downward-sloping symmetrical tusks, uniquely calm disposition around humans.

item.title: Barana of Kala Wewa (බරණ)
item.description: A dominant wild patriarch tusker of the Kala Wewa basin. Renowned among rangers and wildlife enthusiasts for his bold presence and companionship with tusker Revatha. Roaming territory: Kala Wewa, Galkiriyagama, North Central Province. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Heavy thickset tusks, prominent shoulder crest, ruler of the tank shores during dry season gatherings.

item.title: Podi Dala Poottuwa (ගල්ගමුවේ පොඩි දළ පූට්ටුවා)
item.description: Carries the rare crossed-tusk genetics of the fallen legend Galgamuwa Dala Poottuwa. Symbolizes hope and natural renewal for wild tuskers in the northwestern dry zone. Roaming territory: Reswehera Forest Reserve, North Western Province. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Young emergent crossed tusks, alert wild temperament, protected by local community guardians.

item.title: Sumedha of Wasgamuwa (සුමේධ)
item.description: A celebrated wild bull with long sweeping ivory tusks, famous for leading seasonal migrations across Minneriya and Kaudulla reservoirs. Monitored closely by conservationists as a keystone breeder of the Mahaweli river basin. Roaming territory: Wasgamuwa, Minneriya and Kaudulla National Parks. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Long curving ivory tusks, distinctive ear tear notch, calm and cautious demeanor.

item.title: Nandamitra of Yala (නන්දමිත්‍ර)
item.description: Named after ancient King Dutugemunu giant warrior, Nandamitra is a dominant wild tusker of Ruhuna. Frequents the rocky ancient monastic grounds of Sithulpawwa and coastal lagoons of Yala. Roaming territory: Yala National Park and Sithulpawwa Sacred Precinct. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Sharp tapered ivory tusks, tall sturdy back arch, confident approach.

item.title: Kalthota Tusker (Mountain Escarpment Giant) (කල්තොට ඇතා)
item.description: The fabled mountain-foothill wild tusker of the southern central escarpment. Adapted to traversing steep rocky slopes between Uda Walawe and the Horton Plains foothills, inspiring local folk tales. Roaming territory: Kalthota, Balangoda and Uda Walawe, Sabaragamuwa. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Thick curved tusks with ground-sweeping tips, muscular forequarters, elusive nature.

item.title: Somawathiya Sando (සෝමාවතියේ සැන්ඩෝ)
item.description: Named Sando for his colossal body mass and broad muscular build. He is one of the most imposing wild tuskers in the Eastern Province, frequently sighted traversing the sacred Somawathiya marshlands and Mahaweli riverbanks. Roaming territory: Somawathiya National Park, Polonnaruwa. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Massive muscular build, broad forehead, heavy outward-curving tusks.

item.title: Somawathiya Mahasen (සෝමාවතියේ මහසෙන්)
item.description: Named after ancient monarch King Mahasen who built the great tanks. Renowned among researchers for possessing some of the longest and most symmetrical ivory tusks found on any wild elephant in Sri Lanka today. Roaming territory: Somawathiya Sanctuary & Kandakadu, North Central Province. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Extraordinarily long, parallel ivory tusks, tall wild stature, cautious temperament.

item.title: Gemunu of Yala (යාලේ ගැමුණු)
item.description: The most famous and charismatic wild bull elephant in Yala National Park. Known to hundreds of thousands of local and international visitors for gently inspecting safari jeeps for fruit, he is a living legend of the Ruhuna wilderness. Roaming territory: Yala National Park (Ruhuna), Southern Province. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Broad wild physique, ear notches, bold and inquisitive disposition.

item.title: Unicorn of Minneriya (Ekadanta) (මින්නේරියේ යුනිකෝන්)
item.description: The iconic single-tusked dominant bull (Ekadanta) of the great Minneriya Gathering. Recognized immediately by wildlife enthusiasts across the world for his solitary, razor-sharp ivory tusk and undisputed leadership around the Minneriya tank. Roaming territory: Minneriya National Park & Moragaswewa, North Central Province. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Single massive, sharp, upward-curving left tusk, dominant matriarchal escort, towering back ridge.

item.title: Maligawa Raja (The Paramount Casket Bearer) (මාලිගාවේ රාජා)
item.description: The most celebrated temple tusker in modern history. Carried the Sacred Casket of the Tooth Relic at the Kandy Esala Perahera for 37 consecutive years with unmatched majesty and grace. Declared a National Treasure in 1986 by Presidential decree. His preserved remains are enshrined in a dedicated museum within the Dalada Maligawa. Roaming territory: Sri Dalada Maligawa, Kandy. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Two long curving tusks that touched the ground, perfect seven-point posture, exceptional dignity during religious processions.

item.title: Nadungamuwa Raja (නැදුන්ගමුවේ රාජා)
item.description: The revered 10.5-foot tall gentle giant who carried the sacred Casket of the Tooth Relic at the Kandy Esala Perahera for 15 years. He walked over 90 km along national highways from Gampaha to Kandy flanked by military escort and thousands of devotees. Roaming territory: Nadungamuwa, Gampaha and Kandy. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Over 10.5 ft shoulder height, two parallel floor-grazing tusks, calm and dignified demeanor.

item.title: Millangoda Raja (මිල්ලංගොඩ රාජා)
item.description: Renowned for possessing the longest tusks of any Asian elephant in modern history, measuring over 7.5 feet in length that brushed the ground. Carried the sacred tooth relic casket for nearly two decades. Roaming territory: Molagoda, Kegalle and Kandy. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: 7.5 ft sweeping tusks that crossed in front, massive forehead dome, gentle giant of Sabaragamuwa.

item.title: Heiyantuduwa Raja (හෙයියන්තුඩුවේ රාජා)
item.description: Carried the Sacred Relic Casket of the Buddha at the Dalada Maligawa for 11 years following the passing of Maligawa Raja. Also carried the relics at the Kelaniya Duruthu Perahera and Bellanwila Perahera. Roaming territory: Heiyantuduwa, Kelaniya and Kandy. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Broad forehead, upward-sweeping ivory tusks of equal length, regal posture during Buddhist processions.

item.title: Kelani Raja (කැලණි රාජා)
item.description: The chief ceremonial tusker of the Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara for over three decades, bearing the sacred relics across the historic Duruthu Perahera along the banks of the Kelani River. Roaming territory: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara, Gampaha. Status: Deceased. Physical traits: Long downward-tapering tusks, tranquil temper, stately stride during night pageants.

item.title: Muthu Raja (Sak Surin) (මුතු රාජා)
item.description: Gifted by the Royal Family of Thailand to the Government of Sri Lanka in 2001. After decades of service at Kande Vihara, a public advocacy campaign regarding his health led to his historic repatriation to Thailand in July 2023 for intensive medical rehabilitation. Roaming territory: Kande Vihara, Aluthgama and Chiang Mai. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Long sweeping symmetrical ivory tusks, distinct Thai elephant conformation, gentle temperament.

item.title: Kandula the War Tusker (කන්දුල ඇතු)
item.description: The most famous war elephant in ancient Sri Lankan history, documented extensively in the Mahavamsa. Served as the loyal mount of King Dutugemunu, battering through the fortified iron gates of Vijithapura fortress. Roaming territory: Anuradhapura Royal Citadel and Magama Kingdom. Status: Historical. Physical traits: Peerless battle intelligence, immense physical strength, honored with royal ornaments and golden tusk sheaths.

item.title: Kataragama Wasana (වාසනා (කතරගම රාජා))
item.description: The premier ceremonial tusker of the Ruhunu Maha Kataragama Devalaya, carrying the sacred casket of God Skanda through the historic sacred grounds for decades. Roaming territory: Ruhunu Maha Kataragama Devalaya, Monaragala. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Graceful outward-turning tusks, regal demeanor during night torch-lit processions along the Menik Ganga.

item.title: Indiraja of Dalada Maligawa (ඉන්දිරාජා)
item.description: Gifted in 1987 to the Sri Dalada Maligawa by former Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Indiraja is one of the senior ceremonial tuskers trusted to carry the Sacred Relic Casket at the annual Kandy Esala Perahera. Roaming territory: Sri Dalada Maligawa, Kandy. Status: Alive. Physical traits: Tall stature, elegant symmetric tusks, high crown, steady and composed walking gait.
